validated_results.title: Associations of plasma omega-6 and omega-3 fatty acids with overall and 19 site-specific cancers: a population-based cohort study in UK Biobank.
validated_results.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
validated_results.reason: This prospective cohort study from the UK Biobank provides multivariable-adjusted hazard ratios for the association between plasma omega-3 fatty acids and incident prostate cancer.

extraction.population: UK Biobank participants aged 37-73 years without prior cancer at baseline

sample_size.excerpt: A total of 253,138 eligible participants were eventually included.

effect_size.excerpt: In our main models, both omega-6% and omega-3% were inversely associated with overall cancer incidence (HR per SD = 0.98, 95% CI = 0.96–0.99; HR per SD = 0.99, 95% CI = 0.97–1.00; respectively). Of the 19 site-specific cancers available, 14 were associated with omega-6% and five with omega-3%, all indicating inverse associations, with the exception that prostate cancer was positively associated with omega-3% (HR per SD = 1.03, 95% CI = 1.01 – 1.05).

confidence_interval.excerpt: In our main models, both omega-6% and omega-3% were inversely associated with overall cancer incidence (HR per SD = 0.98, 95% CI = 0.96–0.99; HR per SD = 0.99, 95% CI = 0.97–1.00; respectively). Of the 19 site-specific cancers available, 14 were associated with omega-6% and five with omega-3%, all indicating inverse associations, with the exception that prostate cancer was positively associated with omega-3% (HR per SD = 1.03, 95% CI = 1.01 – 1.05).

comparison.excerpt: Risk estimates of the incidence of overall cancer and specific cancer sites for 1-SD increase of plasma omega-6% and omega-3%, for additionally adjusted models.

design.excerpt: We investigated the associations of plasma omega-3 and omega-6 PUFAs with the incidence of overall and 19 site-specific cancers in a large prospective cohort.

timing.excerpt: With a mean follow-up of 12.9 years, 29,838 participants were diagnosed with cancer.

continent.excerpt: Between 2006 and 2010, UK Biobank recruited over half a million participants, aged 37–73, in 22 assessment centers across England, Wales and Scotland.

exposure_measurement.excerpt: The absolute concentrations of plasma polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) were assessed using nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) in plasma samples obtained at the baseline visit from 2007 to 2010, and the corresponding percentages of total fatty acids were calculated
